about: Which weather the fleet downloads (spec: Weather and wind, 'How the location stays private'; engine/src/flight_insights/weather/tiles.py). Each flight's positions are snapped on the laptop to large fixed tiles; the tiles it flew in, and every tile around them, join the download list for good. Only tile names leave the engine, never a position, and only to the shell, which turns each tile into its grid of points for the weather API.
sources: docs/SPEC.md, Weather and wind: 2 by 2 degree tiles plus their neighbours, from the logs on the laptop; the provider learns which large tiles the fleet works in, never a position

min_share: a tile counts when it holds at least 1% of the flight's positions, so a few samples from a GNSS glitch or a spoofed position do not add a tile; a flight crossing into the next tile is covered by the neighbours anyway
gps_min_status: GPS Status 3 is a 3D fix (libraries/AP_GPS/AP_GPS.h GPS_OK_FIX_3D at Copter-4.7.0); GPS positions are used only when the estimator's own (POS) are absent

grids_deg: each model's own resolution. ECMWF IFS HRES is about 9 km on its O1280 reduced Gaussian grid (open data since 1 October 2025, https://openmeteo.substack.com/p/ecmwf-transitions-to-open-data; Open-Meteo serves it on that grid, open-meteo.com/en/docs/ecmwf-api), so points every 0.1 degrees each read their nearest model cell, about one point per cell; the models' effective resolution is several cells, so a finer grid would add requests, not information. ERA5 is on a regular 0.25 degree grid (https://cds.climate.copernicus.eu/datasets/reanalysis-era5-single-levels), which the points match exactly; a 2 degree tile is 20 by 20 = 400 points at 0.1 degrees (its south and west edges and inside; the north and east edges are the next tiles'), within Open-Meteo's 1,000 locations a request (https://openmeteo.substack.com/p/weather-data-for-multiple-locations)

record: the flight is sampled every sample_s along its track. Below the lowest model wind level, the log law with a roughness length z0_m of 0.03 m, open flat terrain (WMO Guide to Instruments and Methods of Observation, WMO-No. 8, Annex 5.B, Davenport classes); temperature carried by the standard atmosphere's lapse rate, 6.5 K/km (ICAO Doc 7488), dew point by about 1.8 K/km; cloud base from the dew-point spread, about 125 m a kelvin (Espy; WMO cloud base estimate); density altitude from virtual temperature with the US National Weather Service's fit to the standard atmosphere (44.3308 - 42.2665 rho^0.234969 km)
